name: OpenCol 0.10.0
body:
OpenCol 0.10.0: **hammers and bells carry over**, and passengers stay aboard their own ship.

| The original | OpenCol 0.10 |
|---|---|
| ![The original: the empty caravel sailed off with the other caravel's colonist](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/blob/v0.10.0/docs/changes/passengers-stay-aboard/before.png?raw=true) | ![OpenCol 0.10 with passengers-stay-aboard on: the caravel that sailed carries nobody, the colonist stays on his own ship](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/blob/v0.10.0/docs/changes/passengers-stay-aboard/after.png?raw=true) |

## New
- **Hammers and bells carry over** (rule option, on at first): hammers past a build's cost and bells past a Founding Father's go to the next one, not thrown away.
- **Passengers stay aboard** (rule option, off at first): ships on one square, or arriving from Europe together, no longer swap passengers. (#8)
- **Each rule option has its own default**: a new `OPENCOL.INI` has custom-house-obeys-boycotts and hammers-and-bells-carry-over on; your own lines stay as they are.

## Download
Unpack the zip for your system where you can write, start `opencol` (`opencol.exe` on Windows 10 or later; macOS 11 or later), and point it at your game's folder once. Coming from 0.9: unpack over the old folder. macOS: right-click > Open the first time.

Limits: Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only; rule options are set in `OPENCOL.INI` (no menu yet); no Linux download, build it from source.

Everything that changed, explained: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/blob/v0.10.0/CHANGELOG.md)

name: OpenCol 0.9.0
body:
OpenCol 0.9.0: **the World View.** The map is drawn whole and shown through a camera: it pans by the pixel, zooms by any amount at the pointer, and fills the window to its edges. Also the full Combat Analysis, and three of the original's trade-route and colony bugs fixed.

OpenCol is *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern program that plays **exactly** like the original unless you turn on a rule option. You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG and Steam): OpenCol contains nothing of the game.

## Play

1. Download the zip for your system below and unpack it **where you can write** (not in `Program Files`).
2. Start the program:
   - **Windows 10 or later:** `opencol.exe` (`windows-x64`; `windows-x86` is the 32-bit one).
   - **macOS 11 or later**, Apple silicon and Intel: `opencol`.
3. The first time, OpenCol asks for the folder of your copy of the game: the one with `VICEROY.EXE` (in the GOG version, the `COLONIZE` folder), or any folder above it. It remembers it.

**Coming from 0.8:** unpack 0.9.0 over your 0.8 folder. Your saved games, maps and settings stay as they are.

**macOS asks first**, because OpenCol is not signed by Apple: right-click `opencol` and choose Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in the folder.

## New

- **World View** (Settings > Display, on at first): the map pans by the pixel (the middle button, the window's edge, two fingers on a Mac) and zooms by any amount at the pointer (the wheel, a pinch), filling the window to its edges, half squares included. The game underneath still moves its view by squares, so the rules see nothing new. **Outside the Map** shows the original's wood past the map's edges, or black.
- **The map fills the window at first**: a wider or larger window shows more of the map, not black bands. Until you choose a UI Scale, OpenCol picks the largest that leaves the screen at least 360 game pixels tall.
- **Combat Analysis in full** (Settings > Interface): every step of both strengths in the order the game applies it, the hidden ones too (the difficulty level's bonus and handicaps, a colonist's halving against soldiers, the Crown's regulars), then each side's combat strength and the attacker's chance to win. **Combat Difficulty** hides the difficulty level's lines.
- **Edge scroll speed**: a slider in Settings > Input, 1 to 10.
- **Longer map names**: up to 31 characters in the editor, Custom Scenario and Import 1994 save, where DOS allowed 8 and an extension.

## Fixed (for everyone, not rule options)

- **Trade routes deliver boycotted goods.** After a Tea Party, a wagon or ship on a route never unloaded the boycotted good and carried it for good. Now it unloads at a colony stop, as unloading by hand does; in Europe it stays aboard, unsold, while the boycott lasts. (#4)
- **100 trade routes**, not the original's 12; past 12 the list scrolls.
- **Ships leave an abandoned colony.** When a colony was abandoned, starved or was disbanded, its ships were left on the land, where they vanished. Now they sail out to the sea beside it with their passengers.

## Limits of this release

- **Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only**: the Roland MT-32 and General MIDI drivers are not supported.
- The colony screen, Europe and the reports keep the original's 320 x 200: their pictures were drawn at that size.
- The rule options have no menu yet: they are set in `OPENCOL.INI`.
- No Linux download: build it from source. Choosing the folder there needs xdg-desktop-portal or zenity; without them, start OpenCol in the game's folder or with `--game FOLDER`.

Every difference from the DOS game, by part of the game and by release, is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). [Open an issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues) for the fixes and features you want.

name: OpenCol 0.8.1
body:
OpenCol 0.8.1: **the music plays every note again.** Many tunes had lost notes, and some (Bird Song, Cornwall, Nightingale) were mostly silence after their first bars.

OpenCol is *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern program that plays **exactly** like the original unless you turn on a rule option. You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG and Steam): OpenCol contains nothing of the game.

## Play

1. Download the zip for your system below and unpack it **where you can write** (not in `Program Files`).
2. Start the program:
   - **Windows 10 or later:** `opencol.exe` (`windows-x64`; `windows-x86` is the 32-bit one).
   - **macOS 11 or later**, Apple silicon and Intel: `opencol`.
3. The first time, OpenCol asks for the folder of your copy of the game: the one with `VICEROY.EXE` (in the GOG version, the `COLONIZE` folder), or any folder above it. It remembers it.

**Coming from 0.8.0:** unpack 0.8.1 over your 0.8.0 folder. Your saved games, maps and settings stay as they are.

**macOS asks first**, because OpenCol is not signed by Apple: right-click `opencol` and choose Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in the folder.

## Fixed

- **The music lost notes, on Windows and macOS alike.** The game's own sound driver plays the music on an emulated AdLib chip. When the driver ended a note and struck the next one in the same instant, the emulated chip missed the change, and the note was not heard again. On a real card a short wait between the two lets the chip see it. Now the emulated chip sees every change, and the tunes play in full.
- The sound driver's timer works as the original's does: it is no longer called a few times at the start when the driver has said it does not need it.

Thanks to the player who reported it.

## Limits of this release

- **Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only**: the Roland MT-32 and General MIDI drivers are not supported.
- The colony screen, Europe and the reports keep the original's 320 x 200: their pictures were drawn at that size.
- The rule options have no menu yet: they are set in `OPENCOL.INI`.
- No Linux download: build it from source. Choosing the folder there needs xdg-desktop-portal or zenity; without them, start OpenCol in the game's folder or with `--game FOLDER`.

Every difference from the DOS game, by part of the game and by release, is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). [Open an issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues) for the fixes and features you want.

name: OpenCol 0.8.0
body:
OpenCol 0.8.0: **long lists scroll** in place of the original's pages, the colonies' start-of-turn messages come on **one Turn Report** in place of a popup each, Congress shows **a card for each Founding Father**, and the map editor makes **scenarios**: roads, units, a start year and each nation's gold, tax and Founding Fathers.

OpenCol is *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern program that plays **exactly** like the original unless you turn on a rule option. You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG and Steam): OpenCol contains nothing of the game.

## Play

1. Download the zip for your system below and unpack it **where you can write** (not in `Program Files`).
2. Start the program:
   - **Windows 10 or later:** `opencol.exe` (`windows-x64`; `windows-x86` is the 32-bit one).
   - **macOS 11 or later**, Apple silicon and Intel: `opencol`.
3. The first time, OpenCol asks for the folder of your copy of the game: the one with `VICEROY.EXE` (in the GOG version, the `COLONIZE` folder), or any folder above it. It remembers it.

**macOS asks first**, because OpenCol is not signed by Apple: right-click `opencol` and choose Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in the folder.

## Coming from 0.7

Unpack 0.8 over your 0.7 folder, or copy 0.7's files into the new one. Your saved games now go in a **`saves`** folder and your maps in a **`maps`** folder, beside the program: the first start moves 0.7's there. The `rules = ...` line of `OPENCOL.INI` becomes a `[Rules]` section, a line for each option with its description.

Coming from 0.6 or earlier: copy the `COLONYnn.SVX` files from `%APPDATA%\OpenCol` (Windows) or `~/Library/Application Support/OpenCol` (macOS) into `saves`, and your maps into `maps`.

## What's new

**Long lists scroll**, smoothly, with the wheel, the scroll bar and the keys, in place of the original's pages: the Naval, colony, trade and labor reports, the Village Adviser, the long popups (the map list, Go to, the trade routes past the original's 12), and the sidebar's units on a square, every one listed in place of "+ More +". Esc leaves a report; OK or Enter goes on to its next part. The labor report's page for a specialty lists every colony, not the first 30.

**Turn Report** (off at first, *Settings > Interface*): the colonies' start-of-turn messages on one page, the worst first, in place of a popup each. A click opens the colony; Shift+F10 shows it again.

**Founding Fathers**: when Congress chooses the next one, a card for each candidate with his face, what he does, and for eight of them what he would change for you now.

**On the map**
- **The go-to route** is exactly the one the unit will take, and keeps off other nations' units.
- **Village notes**: a faded good is one the village would refuse today.
- **Village Adviser**: the scouted villages first, each drawn as the map draws it.

**The map editor**
- **Scenarios**: the Place menu places **Roads** (and plowing) and **Units**; **Start Year...** and **Nations...** set the year and each nation's gold, tax and Founding Fathers. A new game on the map makes them.
- A new map's **width and height**, Generate's size, **Resize Map...** with Undo, and a typed seed.
- **The mouse as on the game's map**: the wheel zooms at the pointer, the middle button drags, the edge scrolls; **Paint Without Shift**.

**A third rule option**, `colonists-may-leave-stockades`: colonists may leave a colony behind walls, and the last one abandons it, as in FreeCol; the original keeps 3 behind a stockade, fort or fortress. Like the others it is off at first; turn it on in the `[Rules]` section of `OPENCOL.INI`.

**The rules stay the original's** unless you turn on an option: the tests replay the computer-only games, the War of Independence and the scripted sessions, and every turn and every saved game is identical to the original's. For contributors: the game record, the nations, the settlements, the counts and the map's planes now live in OpenCol's own memory, as the units did in 0.7.

Every difference from the DOS game, by part of the game and by release, is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Limits of this release

- **Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only**: the Roland MT-32 and General MIDI drivers are not supported.
- The colony screen, Europe and the reports keep the original's 320 x 200: their pictures were drawn at that size.
- The rule options have no menu yet: they are set in `OPENCOL.INI`.
- No Linux download: build it from source. Choosing the folder there needs xdg-desktop-portal or zenity; without them, start OpenCol in the game's folder or with `--game FOLDER`.

[Open an issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues) for the fixes and features you want.

name: OpenCol 0.7.0
body:
OpenCol 0.7.0: **each copy of OpenCol keeps everything in its own folder**, settings in a readable `OPENCOL.INI`, and the map tells you more while you drag a move: the pointer says what the move does, and the go-to route no longer gives away what the fog hides.

OpenCol is *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern program that plays **exactly** like the original unless you turn on a rule option. You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG and Steam): OpenCol contains nothing of the game.

## Play

1. Download the zip for your system below and unpack it **where you can write** (not in `Program Files`).
2. Start the program:
   - **Windows 10 or later:** `opencol.exe` (`windows-x64`; `windows-x86` is the 32-bit one).
   - **macOS 11 or later**, Apple silicon and Intel: `opencol`.
3. The first time, OpenCol asks for the folder of your copy of the game: the one with `VICEROY.EXE` (in the GOG version, the `COLONIZE` folder), or any folder above it. It remembers it.

**macOS asks first**, because OpenCol is not signed by Apple: right-click `opencol` and choose Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in the folder.

## Coming from 0.6 or earlier

OpenCol now keeps your saved games, maps, settings and log **in its own folder**, beside the program, and no longer in `%APPDATA%\OpenCol` (Windows), `~/Library/Application Support/OpenCol` (macOS) or `~/.local/share/OpenCol` (Linux). Two copies of OpenCol can play two copies of the game, and a copy on a USB stick takes everything with it. If OpenCol cannot write to its folder, it says so and stops.

To keep playing your games, copy the `COLONYnn.SVX` files (and your maps, and `OPENCOL.CFG` if you like) from the old folder into OpenCol's folder. The first start turns an `OPENCOL.CFG` into an `OPENCOL.INI` and leaves the old file as it was.

## What's new

**`OPENCOL.INI`.** The settings are now a text file in sections (`[Display]`, `[Sound]`, `[Interface]`...), one `name = value` a line, each explained by the comment above it. Change it while OpenCol is closed: your comments and spacing are kept. The rule options are the `rules` line of `[New Game]`:

    rules = custom-house-obeys-boycotts:1,ai-loads-what-it-plans:1

**The pointer says what a move does.** While you drag a unit, the pointer over the square next to it shows **talk** (a scout at a village or a foreign colony, or a battle the game opens with a question), **attack**, or **landfall** (a ship carrying passengers onto the shore) in place of the original's "TO". *Settings > Interface > Action Cursors* turns it off.

**The go-to route**
- **Tells nothing of what the fog hides.** Into unexplored land, the route drawn is the one you would plan from what your nation has seen, grey where the fog lies, with a "?" on the target. It used to show a hidden lake by bending round it.
- **Marks in yellow where something happens:** boarding or leaving a ship, a Lost City Rumour, a village, a foreign unit or colony. A land unit dragged onto its ship by the coast is now routed onto it.

**Village notes**: of the three goods a chief wants, the one he badly needs is drawn in full colour and the other two faded, in the sidebar and in the Village Adviser.

**The rules stay the original's** unless you turn on an option. The tests replay the computer-only games, the War of Independence and the scripted sessions, with the action cursors on too, and every turn and every saved game is identical to the original's. For contributors: every unit now lives in OpenCol's own memory, past the original's 1 MB (the original's 301 units kept as its view for the tests).

## Limits of this release

- **Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only**: the Roland MT-32 and General MIDI drivers are not supported.
- The colony screen, Europe and the reports keep the original's 320 x 200: their pictures were drawn at that size.
- Two rule options so far, and no menu for them: they are set in `OPENCOL.INI`.
- On Linux (built from source), choosing the folder needs xdg-desktop-portal or zenity; without them, start OpenCol in the game's folder or with `--game FOLDER`.

[Open an issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues) for the fixes and features you want.

name: OpenCol 0.6.0
body:
OpenCol 0.6.0: **the first rule options**, saved games and maps with room to grow, a map editor that places everything, and a lot more comfort on the map: edge scrolling, wheel zoom, Quick Save, the go-to route drawn as you drag.

OpenCol is *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern program that plays **exactly** like the original unless you turn on a rule option. You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG and Steam): OpenCol contains nothing of the game.

## Play

1. Download the zip for your system below and unpack it.
2. Start the program from anywhere:
   - **Windows 10 or later:** `opencol.exe` (`windows-x64`; `windows-x86` is the 32-bit one).
   - **macOS 11 or later**, Apple silicon and Intel: `opencol`.
3. The first time, OpenCol asks for the folder of your copy of the game: the one with `VICEROY.EXE` (in the GOG version, the `COLONIZE` folder), or any folder above it. It remembers it.

**macOS asks first**, because OpenCol is not signed by Apple: right-click `opencol` and choose Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in the folder.

## What's new

**Rule options.** Fixes for the original's bugs and changes to its rules come as options, each off unless you turn it on. There is no menu for them yet: name them on one line of `OPENCOL.CFG`, in OpenCol's folder, while OpenCol is closed:

    rules=custom-house-obeys-boycotts:1,ai-loads-what-it-plans:1

- **custom-house-obeys-boycotts** ([#19](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues/19)): a Custom House keeps a boycotted good in store and sells it again once the boycott ends.
- **ai-loads-what-it-plans**: a computer player's ship or wagon train loads what its plan says, not up to 100 of a good whatever it planned.

A new game takes the options on that line and keeps them to its end, in its saved games too. A 1994 saved game plays by the original's rules.

**Saved games and maps.** OpenCol now saves games as `.SVX` and maps as `.MPX`, with room for what the 1994 files cannot hold. It still loads every 1994 saved game and map: they are in the list marked **(1994)**, and **Import 1994 save...** loads any other `.SAV`. A slot that cannot be loaded says why. The 1994 game cannot load the new files.

**On the map**
- **The map scrolls** when the pointer rests at the window's edge, follows the middle button when you drag, and the **wheel zooms**.
- **The go-to route is drawn** while you drag a unit: the squares it will step through, where each turn ends, and where it would stop short. A unit already on its way shows its route when the pointer rests on it.
- **Quick Save and Quick Load**: Ctrl+S and Ctrl+L. **Keep the last 10 turns' autosaves** lets you go back up to ten turns.
- **Exit to Main Menu** in the GAME menu, and on Esc: exit without saving, save first, or keep playing.
- **Village notes** (first version): the sidebar shows what you have learned about a village, what it teaches, sells and wants, and **REPORTS > Village Adviser** (Shift+F9) lists them all.

**Settings** has five pages now: Display, Sound, Input, Interface and Saves. New in them: **Music and Sound volume** sliders, the edge scroll, middle-button drag and wheel zoom switches, and **Stretch** to fill a large window. The first window is as large as fits your display, sharp on high-DPI screens.

**The main menu** is New Game, Load Game, Settings, Map Editor, Hall of Fame and Exit. **New Game > America** starts the America map at once; **Custom Scenario** plays the maps you make or download.

**The map editor**
- A **Place** menu puts resources, rumours, villages and each nation's start square on the map, not only terrain; **From a Seed...** fills resources and rumours as the game would.
- More steps of **Undo** and **Redo**, a check of the map before saving, and **Export Map as PNG**.
- **Play This Map in Game**, and **Return to Map Editor** from that game.
- It starts with a choice: a new empty map, an existing one, or a random New World.
- Maps may be larger than the original's 12,000 squares, up to 228 squares a side. OpenCol plays them; the 1994 game cannot.

**When something goes wrong**, OpenCol now says so. Every run is logged in `OPENCOL.LOG`, in OpenCol's folder, and a stop on an error writes a `CRASH-...txt` report and offers to open the folder. Attach both to an [issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues/new), with a saved game from just before.

## Fixed

- A map that does not load says why, in the game and in the editor.
- Three places where the 1994 code relied on what its own compiler happened to do (text shifted over itself in menus and popups, among them), found by playing long games under sanitizers, now do what the original did on every compiler.

For contributors: the code has typed accessors for units, nations and the map in place of raw masks, a typed API for new features (`src/port/api.h`), a README in every source folder, a gettext text catalogue, and a contributor guide that needs only your copy of the game. The tests check every change against the original turn by turn, now also through golden hashes anyone can run.

**Without rule options, the rules stay the original's.** The tests replay the computer-only games, the War of Independence and the scripted sessions, and every turn and every saved game is identical to the original's.

## Limits of this release

- **Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only**: the Roland MT-32 and General MIDI drivers are not supported.
- The colony screen, Europe and the reports keep the original's 320 x 200: their pictures were drawn at that size.
- Two rule options so far, and no menu for them yet.
- On Linux (built from source), choosing the folder needs xdg-desktop-portal or zenity; without them, start OpenCol in the game's folder or with `--game FOLDER`.

name: Test data: reference saves 1
body:
Not a game release. Test data for contributors.

`opencol-test-saves-1.tar.xz` holds every saved game the original game wrote while the lockstep recordings were made: 7,906 saves from 71 recordings (221 MB unpacked). They are player files, not the game's data. With them, `tests/golden/golden.py check` compares a saved game that differs with the original's, record by record and field by field.

    build/venv/bin/python tests/golden/golden.py fetch-saves

downloads it, checks it against `tests/golden/saves.txt` (sha256 01e29ba41b0aee68fd653851300b5f4722f49c6d79aae128cbcc3e806f8762dc) and unpacks it into `build/golden-saves/`. See CONTRIBUTING.md, "Without the recordings".

name: OpenCol 0.5.1
body:
OpenCol 0.5.1: **the Windows version no longer freezes on the Colonopedia's terrain pages**, and a copy of OpenCol can keep its own settings.

OpenCol is *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern program that plays **exactly** like the original, with the 1994 map editor built in. You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG and Steam): OpenCol contains nothing of the game.

## Play

1. Download the zip for your system below and unpack it.
2. Start the program from anywhere:
   - **Windows 10 or later:** `opencol.exe` (`windows-x64`; `windows-x86` is the 32-bit one).
   - **macOS 11 or later**, Apple silicon and Intel: `opencol`.
3. The first time, OpenCol asks for the folder of your copy of the game: the one with `VICEROY.EXE` (in the GOG version, the `COLONIZE` folder), or any folder above it. It remembers it.

**macOS asks first**, because OpenCol is not signed by Apple: right-click `opencol` and choose Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in the folder.

## Fixed

- **Windows: the game froze on a terrain's page in the Colonopedia** (F1 on the map, for one), and had to be closed. The Windows programs are built with another compiler than the macOS one, and it read one of the game's tables, declared shorter than the game uses it, as a loop without an end. The table has its full length now, and the tests run every game and session on a build by that compiler too, so this kind of difference is caught before a release.

## What's new

- **An `OPENCOL.CFG` beside the program is used first**, before the one in OpenCol's own folder: a copy of OpenCol, on a USB stick say, can keep its settings and its game of its own.
- For contributors: the code is easier to read and change. The longest functions of the game (the computer players' moves and colonies, combat, the natives, diplomacy) read as named steps; the game's memory has a typed layout; every part has its own header; and the code builds without warnings. None of it changes the game: the tests compare every step with the original.

**The rules stay the original's.** The tests replay the computer-only games, the War of Independence and the scripted sessions, and every turn and every saved game is identical to the original's.

## Limits of this release

- **Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only**: the Roland MT-32 and General MIDI drivers are not supported.
- The colony screen, Europe and the reports keep the original's 320 x 200: their pictures were drawn at that size.
- On Linux (built from source), choosing the folder needs xdg-desktop-portal or zenity; without them, start OpenCol in the game's folder or with `--game FOLDER`.
- **No changes to the game's rules yet.** Fixes and new features come next; [open an issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues) for the ones you want.

name: OpenCol 0.5.0: start it from anywhere
body:
OpenCol 0.5.0: **start it from anywhere**. OpenCol finds your copy of the game, or asks for it once, and keeps your saved games and settings in its own folder.

OpenCol is *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern program that plays **exactly** like the original, with the 1994 map editor built in. You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG and Steam): OpenCol contains nothing of the game.

## Play

1. Download the zip for your system below and unpack it.
2. Start the program from anywhere:
   - **Windows 10 or later:** `opencol.exe` (`windows-x64`; `windows-x86` is the 32-bit one).
   - **macOS 11 or later**, Apple silicon and Intel: `opencol`.
3. The first time, OpenCol asks for the folder of your copy of the game: the one with `VICEROY.EXE` (in the GOG version, the `COLONIZE` folder), or any folder above it. It remembers it.

**macOS asks first**, because OpenCol is not signed by Apple: right-click `opencol` and choose Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in the folder.

## What's new

- **No more copying OpenCol into the game's folder.** OpenCol looks for the game where it is started and where it sits, then in the folder it remembers; otherwise it asks, with your system's folder picker. You may pick the install folder: OpenCol finds `VICEROY.EXE` below it.
- **Your saved games and settings have their own folder**, and the game's folder is never changed:
  - macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/OpenCol`
  - Windows: `%APPDATA%\OpenCol`
  - Linux: `~/.local/share/OpenCol`
- **Nothing is lost from 0.4.** The saved games in the game's folder (the original's, or an earlier OpenCol's) are still in the list to load; saving one again writes it to OpenCol's folder. Your `OPENCOL.CFG` is copied over on the first start.
- To play another copy of the game, delete the `game=` line from `OPENCOL.CFG`, or start `opencol --game FOLDER` (for that run). `--save FOLDER` still keeps the saved games elsewhere.

**The rules stay the original's.** The tests replay the computer-only games, the War of Independence and the scripted sessions, and every turn and every saved game is identical to the original's.

## Limits of this release

- **Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only**: the Roland MT-32 and General MIDI drivers are not supported.
- The colony screen, Europe and the reports keep the original's 320 x 200: their pictures were drawn at that size.
- On Linux (built from source), choosing the folder needs xdg-desktop-portal or zenity; without them, start OpenCol in the game's folder or with `--game FOLDER`.
- **No changes to the game's rules yet.** Fixes and new features come next; [open an issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues) for the ones you want.

name: OpenCol 0.4.0: more of the map, and Settings
body:
OpenCol 0.4.0: **more of the map on a larger screen**, and **Settings** in the game's menus.

OpenCol is *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern program that plays **exactly** like the original, with the 1994 map editor built in. You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG and Steam): OpenCol contains nothing of the game.

## Play

1. Download the zip for your system below and unpack it.
2. Put the program into the folder of your copy of the game, the one with `VICEROY.EXE` (in the GOG version, the `COLONIZE` folder):
   - **Windows 10 or later:** `opencol.exe` (`windows-x64`; `windows-x86` is the 32-bit one).
   - **macOS 11 or later**, Apple silicon and Intel: `opencol`.
3. Start it there. The game saves its games in that folder, as the original does.

**macOS asks first**, because OpenCol is not signed by Apple: right-click `opencol` and choose Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in the folder.

## What's new

**Settings**, in the main menu and in the GAME menu while you play:

- **Display, Screen Size**: how much of the map you see. The original's 320 x 200 shows 15 x 12 squares; 640 x 400 shows 35 x 24, 800 x 600 shows 45 x 37, and 1280 x 800 the map's whole width, or choose **Fill the window**. The menu bar and the sidebar fill the screen, and the sidebar lists more of a stack.
- **Display, UI Scale**: how big it all is on your screen, 1x to 6x. A larger Screen Size keeps everything the same size and shows more map; a larger UI Scale makes everything bigger. Full screen keeps the size you chose.
- **Display, Screens**: the colony, Europe, the reports and the Colonopedia open in a window over the map, which stays visible around them, dimmed; or on their own.
- **Display, Pixels**: square, or as tall as a 1994 monitor showed them (4:3).
- **Game Options, Colony Report Options, Sound Options**: the original's, moved here from the GAME menu. In the main menu they set the options every new game starts with.

OpenCol starts at 320 x 200 and 2x, and remembers your choices in `OPENCOL.CFG`, beside your saved games. On the command line: `--resolution 800x600`, `--fit`, `--scale 3`, `--aspect 4:3`.

**The rules stay the original's at every size.** The tests replay 52 computer-only games, the War of Independence and the scripted sessions with the larger map, and with its size changed every turn, and every turn and every saved game is identical to the original's.

## Fixed since 0.3.1

- On a larger screen, a full-screen picture (a woodcut, a report) could draw the mouse pointer outside the screen and spoil the palette: wrong colours from then on.
- Alt on its own opens the GAME menu again, instead of crashing.

## Limits of this release

- **Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only**: the Roland MT-32 and General MIDI drivers are not supported.
- The colony screen, Europe and the reports keep the original's 320 x 200: their pictures were drawn at that size.
- **No changes to the game's rules yet.** Fixes and new features come next; [open an issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues) for the ones you want.

name: OpenCol 0.3.0: the map editor, built in
body:
OpenCol 0.3.0 brings the 1994 **map editor** into the game.

OpenCol is *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern program that plays **exactly** like the original. You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG and Steam): OpenCol contains nothing of the game.

## What's new

- **The map editor, built in.** The main menu has a new last item, **Open the MAP EDITOR**. The original's own editor (MAPEDIT.EXE, rebuilt as [OpenCol/mapedit](https://github.com/OpenCol/mapedit)) opens in the game's window; leave it and you are back at the menu. No second program, no second window.
- The editor reads and saves maps in your game's folder, as the original did. Saving `AMER2.MP` changes the map *Start a Game in AMERICA* plays on; to keep the original, give your map a new name (Escape on the editor's first screen makes a new map).

## Play

1. Download the zip for your system below and unpack it.
2. Put what it contains into the folder of your copy of the game, the one with `VICEROY.EXE` (in the GOG version, the `COLONIZE` folder):
   - **Windows:** `opencol.exe` and `SDL2.dll` (`windows-x64` for 64-bit Windows, `windows-x86` for 32-bit).
   - **macOS:** `opencol` and `SDL2.framework`.
3. Start `opencol`.

**macOS asks first**, because OpenCol is not signed by Apple: right-click `opencol` and choose Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in the folder.

F11 or Alt+Enter switches to full screen; `--no-sound` plays without sound. On Linux, build from source (see the README).

## Still exactly the original

The 71 recorded scenarios (51,711 checkpoints: the whole game state, every screen, every saved game) are still identical with the original, and 495 functions still match its machine code one by one. The editor's item is OpenCol's only addition to the menus.

## Limits of this release

- **Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only**, as in 0.2.0: the Roland MT-32 and General MIDI drivers are not supported.
- **No changes to the game's rules yet.** Fixes and new features come next; [open an issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues) for the ones you want.

name: OpenCol 0.2.0: sound, Windows, no setup
body:
OpenCol 0.2.0 brings sound and music, ready-made builds for Windows, and no more command line: put OpenCol into your game's folder and start it.

OpenCol is *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern program that plays **exactly** like the original. You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG and Steam): OpenCol contains nothing of the game.

## What's new

- **Sound and music.** The original's own Sound Blaster driver plays the AdLib music and the digitized sound effects, on an emulated card. `--no-sound` plays without.
- **Windows**, 64-bit and 32-bit, and **macOS** for both Apple silicon and Intel.
- **No setup.** Put OpenCol into the folder of your game (the one with `VICEROY.EXE`) and start it. It saves its games there, as the original does. `--game FOLDER` still works from anywhere.
- One program to play, `opencol`. The window-less one the tests use is no longer in the download.

## Play

1. Download the zip for your system below and unpack it.
2. Put what it contains into the folder of your copy of the game, the one with `VICEROY.EXE` (in the GOG version, the `COLONIZE` folder):
   - **Windows:** `opencol.exe` and `SDL2.dll` (`windows-x64` for 64-bit Windows, `windows-x86` for 32-bit).
   - **macOS:** `opencol` and `SDL2.framework`.
3. Start `opencol`.

**macOS asks first**, because OpenCol is not signed by Apple: right-click `opencol` and choose Open, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine .` in the folder.

F11 or Alt+Enter switches to full screen. On Linux, build from source (see the README).

## Still exactly the original

The 71 recorded scenarios (51,711 checkpoints: the whole game state, every screen, every saved game) are still identical with the original, and 495 functions still match its machine code one by one. The Windows, macOS Intel and macOS Apple silicon builds write the same saved games, byte for byte.

As in the original, a game with music is a little different every time: when a tune ends, the game reseeds its random numbers.

## Limits of this release

- **The Sound Blaster and AdLib sound only.** The original's Roland MT-32 and General MIDI drivers are not supported: OpenCol always plays the Sound Blaster's, whatever your `CONFIG.COL` says.
- **No changes to the game yet.** This release is the original, bugs included. Fixes and new features come next; [open an issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues) for the ones you want.

name: OpenCol 0.1.0
body:
The first release of OpenCol: *Sid Meier's Colonization* for DOS (version 3.0, February 1995), decompiled and rebuilt as a modern C++ program that plays **exactly** like the original.

You need your own copy of the DOS game (as sold by GOG or Steam): OpenCol reads the game's files from it and contains nothing of the game.

## What you get

- `opencol-sdl`: the game in a window, played with the keyboard and the mouse. The window scales by whole multiples; F11 or Alt+Enter switches to full screen.
- `opencol`: the same game without a window, used by the tests.
- Saved games are byte for byte the original's, so the two load each other's saves.

## How it is proven identical

The original game runs in DOSBox-X, made deterministic, and records checkpoints. The port runs the same scenario and must match at every one of them:
- the whole data segment, the map and the random number generator's position;
- every screen the player sees, pixel by pixel, before each key and mouse step of a scripted session;
- every saved game the original writes, byte for byte.

The corpus:
- AI-only games from 52 seeds, from 1492 to the 1720s;
- the War of Independence played from a saved game, to 1755;
- human sessions with the keyboard and the mouse: the new game and its options, the map, the colony screen, Europe, the reports, Colonopedia, trade routes, the menus, saving, declaring independence and fighting the war, retiring.

That is 71 recordings and 51,711 checkpoints, all identical. 495 functions are also compared one by one with the original's machine code, and agree. See [STATUS.md](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/blob/main/STATUS.md) and [docs/port.md](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/blob/main/docs/port.md).

## Limits of this release

- **No sound or music yet.** The game runs as with no sound card.
- **Binary for macOS on Apple silicon only** (macOS 12 or later). On Linux and other systems, build from source: CMake, clang or GCC, and SDL2 for the window (see [docs/port.md](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/blob/main/docs/port.md)).
- **No changes to the game yet.** This release is the original, bugs included. Fixes and new features come next, each one deliberate; [open an issue](https://github.com/OpenCol/OpenCol/issues) for the ones you want.

## macOS: getting started

```
brew install sdl2
tar xzf opencol-0.1.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz
cd opencol-0.1.0-macos-arm64
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine opencol opencol-sdl
./opencol-sdl --exe GAME/VICEROY.EXE --game GAME --save SAVES
```

`GAME` is the folder of your copy (the one with `VICEROY.EXE`). `SAVES` is any folder for the saved games: the game reads its files from `GAME` and writes only into `SAVES`.
